sasha: Quick perf thread — ran an end-to-end profile for the new KV shard policy `layer-striped` on 8xA100 (TP=2 PP=2 DP=1), seq=256, batch_tokens ~ 8192.

sasha: Command I used:
```
./profile --model=resnet-llm-v2 --seq=256 --shots=200 --tp=2 --pp=2 --dp=1 --kv-shard=layer-striped --trace perf.trace
```

sasha: Summary numbers (avg per step): total=112ms, compute=68ms, allreduce=28ms, memcpy=9ms, kernel-fallbacks=7ms. Observed a spike around layer 14 where allreduce jumps to ~85ms for that step.

leo: can you paste the perf trace snippet? curious if the allreduce time is single large call or many tiny calls piling up.

sasha: pasted short excerpt from trace (trimmed):
```
layer13: matmul_attn 10ms -> ncclAllReduce 6ms
layer14: matmul_attn 12ms -> ncclAllReduce 85ms  # huge spike
layer15: matmul_attn 11ms -> ncclAllReduce 5ms
```

maya: @sasha interesting — looks like kernel-selector fell back to a slower attention path for layer14 (we saw that before when quantized weights missed the fast matmul kernel). fallback + an unlucky allreduce alignment can blow up. Did the trace show any kernel mismatch logs?

sasha: yes there was a "kernel_selector: fallback matmul_generic" log right before layer14. Also noticed small variations in sequence length distribution for that micro-batch which may have prevented batching/overlap.

ahmed: from the NCCL side, I pulled the per-rank timeline: rank0 blocked on `ncclAllReduce` waiting for rank3 for ~72ms — the pattern looks like straggler on one GPU (possibly due to fallback running on a different SM/kernel).

maya: two quick mitigations to try: 1) force the fast kernel for attention on suspect layers via `kernel_selector.force=matmul_fast` (can be toggled per-layer), 2) reduce the batching window so we don't aggregate the micro-batch that triggers the slow path (e.g., lower max_tokens). Either should shrink the allreduce tail.

sasha: good call. i'll run a canary with:
```
kernel_selector.force=matmul_fast
batching.max_tokens=4096
kv_cache.shard_policy=hybrid  # replicate early layers, stripe later
```
and report back.

perf-bot: perf-check: regression trace linked to commit abc1234 (kernel-selector heuristic change). marking high-priority.

leo: if the hybrid policy helps, we should add a perf-test that runs TP/PP combos to catch this pattern. all-reduce straggler tests are cheap to add.

sasha: agreed — i'll run the canary now and post updated numbers. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:
